![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215565/assets/eec7d2b67f0b76bb8ec6874cf63f8cb09005f451d684924118983ea1aa39269c.png)

The $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ on the curve $y=\ln \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$ that is closest to the origin (as shown above) satisfies the equation 

$$
2x + \bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAA^2}}=0.
$$

 
What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
Let's consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(0,0)$ and a general point $P(x, y)\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x,y) & =(x-0)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y=\ln \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right).$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{x}))}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+{ln}^{2}⁡(\frac{1}{x})\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(x)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(x)=2x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{x})\cdot \frac{1}{(\frac{1}{x})}\cdot (-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}) & =0 \\ 2x-\frac{2}{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{x}) & =0 \\ 2x-\frac{2}{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡x) & =0 \\ 2x+\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing expression is $\dfrac{2\ln x}{x}.$
